senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. תָּפַף)to seize, take hold on; to take effect.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 84b:12">Keth. 84ᵇ</cite> <he>את תּוֹפֵס לבעל חוב וכ׳</he> thou seizest property in behalf of a creditor when the debtor owes others, <he>ואמר ר׳ י׳ התופס וכ׳</he> and R. J. has decided that he who seizes in behalf of a creditor when there are other claimants has not taken legal possession.
<cite ref="Ketubot 84b:12">Ib.</cite> top <he>והוא שת׳ מחיים</he> (his possession is effectual) when he has seized it during the decedent’s life-time.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 8b:4">Ab. Zar. 8ᵇ</cite> (expl. <cite ref="S02004"><he>קרטיסיס</he></cite>) <he>יום שתָּפְסָה בו רומי מלכות</he> the day when Rome took hold of the government (of the east, v. <cite ref="V00821"><he>תְּפִיסָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5:2">Y. Taan. IV, 68ᶜ</cite> top <he>היה משה תוֹפְשָׂן</he> Moses held fast on them (the tablets).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 4b:15">R. Hash. 4ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>תָּפַסְתָּ מרובה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M00561"><he>מוּעָט</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 102b:9">B. Mets. 102ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>תְּפוֹס לשון אחרון</he> hold to the latter expression, i.e. if an agreement contains two discrepant clauses, the second is legally recognized; <cite ref="Temurah 26a">Tem. 26ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>תפוס לשון ראשון</he> the first clause (of a vow) is legally recognized.
<cite ref="Yevamot 10b">Yeb. 10ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אין קידושין תּוֹפְסִין וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="S00873"><he>קִידּוּשׁ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 6:1:8">Y. Dem. VI, 25ᵇ</cite> <he>תָּפְשָׂה מדת הדין וכ׳</he> justice takes hold on him &c., i.e. the full rigor of the law is applied against him &c.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 11">Num. R. s. 11<sup>1</sup></cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 3:34">Prov. III, 34</cite>) <he>אלו הנזירים שתּוֹפְשִׂים ענוה בעצמן וכ׳</he> that means the Nazarites who choose humility for themselves, who abstain from wine &c. Ib. 10<sup>8</sup> <he>ותְפָשָׂם</he> and arrested them, v. <cite ref="L00310"><he>לוּפָר</he></cite>.
Snh. 64ᵃ מפני מה תפסה תורה לשון מולך why does the Biblical text choose the word Molekh (in place of idol in general)? Y. Ber. VII, 11ᶜ top, a. e. תופסין אותו seize him, take him to task, v. נַקְדָּן.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 64a:6-8">Ab. Zar. 64ᵃ</cite> <he>דמי … מי תוֹפֶסֶת דמיה וכ׳</he> how about money which was realized by the sale of an idol, in the hands of a gentile? does the idol hold its equivalent in gentile hands or not?, i.e. does the money in gentile hands retain its character as compensation for an idol, and is it thus forbidden to a Jew? <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ex. R. s. 15<sup>20</sup></cite> <he>היה שלמה תופס פיו וכ׳</he> Solomon controlled his mouth, in order not to speak before &c.

Gen. R. s. 12 כל … תופסין את הלשון וזה אינו תופס וכ׳ all other letters catch the tongue (require an effort of the organs of speech), but this (the Hé) does not catch &c. (is merely a breathing sound).—Part. pass. תָּפוּס, תָּפוּשׂ; f. תְּפוּסָה, תְּפוּשָׂה &c.

senses.gloss: (cmp. אָחוּז s. v. אָחַז) holding. Y. Taan. l. c. היה משה ת׳ בטפחיים Moses was holding two handbreadths (of the tablets).
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 46">Ex. R. s. 46</cite>, beg. <he>היה ת׳ בלוחות וכ׳</he> he held the tablets, and would not believe that Israel had sinned. Sifra B’ḥuck. Par. 2, ch. VIII <he>תְּפוּסֵי מעשה וכ׳</he> holding to the deeds of their fathers, generation after generation; a. e.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: seized, captured. Mekh. Mishp., s. 17 תפוסה the outraged woman, opp. מפותה the seduced.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to be seized, arrested; to have one’s property seized; to be made responsible.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ex. R. s. 15<sup>18</sup></cite> <he>בן בית שנ׳ על ידי בעל וכ׳</he> a domestic servant who was seized for his employer’s debt.
<cite ref="Tosefta Chullin 2:24">Tosef. Ḥull. II, 24</cite> <he>נ׳ ע״ד מינות</he>, v. <cite ref="M01219"><he>מִינוּת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Chullin 2:24">Ib.</cite> <he>ונִתְפַּסְתִּי על וכ׳</he> and therefore I was arrested on the suspicion of heresy.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17b:4">Ab. Zar. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>כשנִתְפְּסוּ ר׳ אלעזר וכ׳</he> when R. El. a. R. H. b. T. were arrested (by Roman officials, for rebellious conduct).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>אשריך שנִתְפַּסְתָּ על וכ׳</he> happy art thou, for thou hast been arrested on one charge only, and woe me that I have been arrested on five charges.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 16b:3">B. Bath. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>אין אדם נ׳ על צערו</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>בשעת</he>) no man is taken to account for what he speaks in his distress.

Sabb. 33ᵇ נִתְפָּסִים על הדור are seized for the debt (die for the sins) of their generation. Y. Keth. XIII, 35ᵈ כל הנ׳ על חבירו חייב ליתן לו in every case if one’s property was seized for a neighbor’s debt, the latter has to reimburse him; ib. אין לך נ׳ וכ׳ in no case must he reimburse him, except in the case of annona and head-tax; Y. B. Kam. X, end, 7ᶜ; Y. Ned. IV, beg. 38ᶜ.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite>, beg. (prov.) <he>הוי זהיר שלא תִתָּפֵס מקום דבורך</he> take care that thou be not caught on the spot where thou speakest (held to thy word); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to cause to be seized, cause to take hold. Y. Succ. IV, 54ᵈ top ראה שהִתְפִּיסָתְךָ התורה לשון וכ׳ behold, the Law has made thee use the expression of endearment &c.
units: <cite ref="Temurah 2a:10">Tem. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>הכל מַתְפִּיסִין בתמורה</he> all persons can cause the seizure of the substitute together with the original by exchanging a consecrated animal (v. <cite ref="V00667"><he>תְּמוּרָה</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Temurah 9a:34">Ib. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>מי מַתְפִּיס בדבר שאינו שלו</he> can one cause the seizure of a thing which is not his?; a. e.—[<cite ref="Nedarim 11b">Ned. 11ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>מתפיס</he>, v. next w.]

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 66">Gen. R. s. 66</cite>, end (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 30:28">Prov. XXX, 28</cite>) <he>באיזה זכות השממית מְתַפֶּשֶׂת בזכות וכ׳</he> for what merit does the spider (Esau-Rome) climb (rise to power)? For the merit of those hands (with which Esau nursed his father, by ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 27:31">Gen. XXVII, 31</cite>); Yalk. ib. 115; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 963:6">Yalk. Prov. 963</cite> <he>תְּתַפֵּשׂ</he>.

senses.gloss: , Hithparel הִתַּרְפֵּס same. Y. Erub. V, 22ᵈ top רואה אותו כי מִיתַּרְפֵּס ועולה מְתַרְפֵּס ויורד, (v. טָפַס) you look upon it (measure the distance for Sabbath purposes) as if one would climb up and climb down (the wady).
